scope: Independent review of only the 13 Baby play/home placements at 6–9 months: exact frozen public prose, age/topic metadata, reference labels, actual rendered opening/topic/detail text and the two opening art contexts. Original source pages were read by this reviewer; author/research logs were not treated as independent reading.

readLogs.description: Complete original-page text for setting up Montessori-style spaces, yes spaces, observe/store/rotate, room-by-room including outside, and older-sibling access. Includes the relevant section continuations; sleep and care examples remain context only.

Complete original-page text for activity, praise, pace, choices, boundaries, concentration, freedom of movement, secure attachment and crying through its comfort checklist. The source’s responsive help and safety limits qualify independent activity; deterministic and clinical claims are not imported.

Complete activity introduction and selection unit, including individual pace, developmental support, object and component suitability, effort/frustration, rotation, infant restoration, adult role, spontaneous exploration and clothing context.

Complete language unit including 0–3, 3–6, 6–9, 9–12 and 12+ prose, the first-books list, the 137–138 language summary/observations, and bilingualism. Cited conversation/naming, music and baby-sign age differences checked in their actual sections.

Complete original-page text from the 3–6 movement introduction through 6–9 and 9–12 movement/fine-motor sections, observations and falls callout, then the complete music and outdoors sections. Relevant visual content is logged separately.

Complete newborn sensory and movement-mat text and its continuation, including awake context, closeness and discomfort, to distinguish the scene and present movement summary from sleep or transfer instructions.

Complete clothing, dressing, diapering and resistance text, including necessary-care override and gentle handling, read as context for the limited movement-positioning claim. Bathing begins at the end but is not relied on.
Complete mouthing question/answer and adjacent original-page text, including the oral-stage and coin assertions held from this object-exploration wording.
Complete Notes for our visitors from our baby, with mouth exploration, removal of unsafe objects, connection, concentration, closeness and proportionate help.

Read all original-page content at readable full-page scale: activity guideline opening and complete tables 295–301, including each age cell, activity name, description and area-of-development column. Checked books/rhythmic language, known-object basket, rolling objects, creeping ball basket, egg/cube/tray boxes, both ring bases and pull-up furniture rows.

Readable original full-page visual inspection: home starter-set labeled illustration; language age/observation list; self-sitting passage and furniture image; complete movement-posture chart and falls callout; complete three-page movement inventory with heading continuations, wooden book, drum, basket, wooden egg/cup, and box variants.

textPlacement.assessment: The Move opening, its attributed awake-movement invitation, observation cue and Read more CTA remain a perspective. Both topic summaries retain help and the specific sitting/standing propping distinction. Full text distinguishes the authors’ back/tummy discussion, comfort and picking up, proportionate help and developmental support; it gives no handling sequence, exercise schedule or guaranteed outcome. The 6–9 placement and earlier 3–6 source context are explicit. Cited original sections support the public claims and PDF references.

artContext.assessment: The actual WebP, current alt/caption and the exact Move opening/full-text context support an awake infant’s interested reach with a nearby adult. The picture shows no sitting/standing propping, restraint, installed apparatus, sleep scene or handling demonstration. Its ball and thin mat remain illustrative context rather than a measured setup or a certified product. This art verdict is bound separately to the current movement text and asset bytes.

The 6–9 placement continues the earlier conversation context, with source ages kept visible and correctly cited.

textPlacement.assessment: Both Play & discovery and Connection & feelings topic rows preserve following an existing look or sound. The complete 6–9 language passage supports the phone, barking dog and held-spoon examples. The detail asks for ordinary naming rather than testing recall or requiring repetition, and the title, cue, age context and PDF p. 135 reference preserve that limited invitation.

Both topic summaries and the full reading view preserve familiar subjects, the baby’s page interest and the possibility of not finishing. Board books and family photographs are supported by the main book list and the all-ages appendix row. The public text does not confuse the separately illustrated wooden book with board-book advice or impose the book’s progression as a deadline. The 6–9 placement retains first-year/all-ages framing and precise PDF references.

Both topic rows offer a brief shared song or listening moment without promising a response. Changing speed or voice, a short rhyme with a gesture, and periods without music are supported by the language passage, full music section and rhythmic-language row. The text leaves instruments optional and distinguishes the 6–9 variation passage from the all-ages appendix context. References and displayed labels match that scope.

Both topic rows and the detail remain ordinary noticing, naming and quiet listening, supported by the complete home Outside and activity Outdoors sections. They do not convert the neighboring transport, positioning, natural-material handling or walking examples into a protocol. First-month source framing is visible without making it a new requirement for the 6–9 browsing placement; PDF references point to the actual passages.

The topic summary attributes the hand-exploration perspective and carries object/component suitability for mouthing. The full view preserves current grasp and transfer, possible help retrieving objects, varied qualities, the rotating drum and interest in containers. Safe finishes, size and attached parts are visible, and natural material is not presented as certification. The earlier grasp context remains distinct from the 6–9 transfer/drum examples; the cited pages and their relevant units support the wording.

Both topic summaries retain independent sitting and object/part suitability. The complete 159–160 passage and appendix p. 299 distinguish a seated discovery basket from two or three familiar toys in a soft basket that may be used lying or sitting. The full view preserves baby choice and occasional naming without authorizing propping or certifying household objects. The 6–9 and 5 or 6+ source labels and PDF locators remain separate and accurate.

The topic summary retains slithering readiness, slow/near rolling, and material/component suitability. The full view preserves handling as well as following, manageable effort, and the appendix’s distinct creeping condition for a basket of balls. Source ages are not silently normalized to the 6–9 browsing band. Complete prose and original appendix rows support the displayed claims and references; no size, construction or product certification is inferred from a picture.

The topic summary explicitly identifies different age/sitting conditions and mouthing-safe pieces with secure parts. The full view supports taking out before returning, the tray-box example, stable sitting for rocking rings and the preceding-skill condition for the stable-base version. Main 9–12 and earlier appendix ages stay visible, making the 6–9 placement a qualified possibility to revisit. This is descriptive material context, with no construction sequence, tiny posting variants or completion expectation; the cited original prose and complete rows support it.

Both home and play topic rows preserve a few current choices and observation-led rotation. The full text retains infant-specific adult restoration and separates accessible baby-suitable objects from older siblings’ small parts. The around-seven-month example is present on cited PDF p. 122; it does not become a required room arrangement. The original home and activity sections support the title, summary, context, detail and displayed references.

Both topic summaries and the detail concern pictures being visible from the baby’s position. Familiar faces, animals, nature, handmade touches and the possibility of a bolder room style are supported by the complete home unit. The 6–9 placement uses interest without inventing a numerical source age. No mounting method, reachable glass/frame specification, display quota or required purchase is supplied; the PDF references are accurate.

Both topic summaries describe the authors’ adapting space to actual access, with removed/secured hazards and self-initiated pulling up. The full view retains the Gerber/RIE attribution, one-area option, secure furniture, inaccessible cords/chemicals and suitable objects. It names the main-text/appendix wall-bar difference without choosing an installation measurement. Readiness and varied source ages qualify the 6–9 placement; the source references and actual short/detail surfaces preserve this descriptive boundary.
